summary: This test verifies that a helper function called `assert::binaryExists` correctly fails when checking for a binary that doesn't exist on the system. It mocks the `which` command to always fail, then checks that the assertion function exits with an error and prints the expected error message.

explanations.3: This creates a fake `which` command inside the test that always exits with status 1 (failure), overriding the real system `which` command so we can simulate a missing binary without actually needing one missing.
explanations.7: The `run` keyword in Bats executes a command and captures its exit status and output so we can make assertions about them afterward.
explanations.16: This sets a default error message if no message was provided as the second argument — it uses the function name and binary name to create a helpful default.
explanations.18: This checks if `which` returns nothing (meaning the binary wasn't found), and if so, prints the error message and exits with status 1 to signal failure; the `|| true` prevents `which` failing from crashing the whole script.
explanations.20: This returns success status (0) only if the binary was actually found by the previous check, so the function succeeds when it should.
